title: POSE — pose_result
description: Frozen contract between the inference pipeline (producer, S-008/S-009) and the 3D viewer (consumer, S-010/S-011). One file per processed scene image. World frame is Z-up, origin = table plane null-point, units = meters. Rotation convention is column: world = R @ body, consistent with the faces_<part>.json registry (faces/cluster_views.py).

source_image.description: Path or filename of the scene image the results were inferred from.

table_origin.description: World-coordinate null-point of the table plane [x, y, z] in meters. The viewer anchors the table to this point.

units.description: Length unit for all translations and table_origin. Frozen to meters.

coordinate_convention.description: Human-readable convention statement. MUST document: Z-up world, column rotation world = R @ body (same as faces_<part>.json registry), origin = table plane null-point.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this contract. Producer and consumer assert compatibility on the major version.

results.description: One entry per detected part instance in the scene.

instance_id.description: Unique id of this part instance within the scene (stable for the viewer to track).

part.description: Part identifier, must match the CAD/registry name (e.g. 'Anker_Lang', 'Zahnrad_Typ7'). Drives model routing and CAD load in the viewer.

face.description: Resting face name as produced by the registry, e.g. 'Face 1'. Matches faces_<part>.json faces[].name.

R_world.description: 3x3 rotation matrix flattened row-major to 9 floats. Column convention: world = R @ body. Consistent with faces_<part>.json faces[].R; the inferred yaw is composed onto the registry rest rotation R_face.

t_world.description: Translation of the part body origin in world coordinates [x, y, z] in meters, relative to the table-plane null-point.

bbox_2d.description: Axis-aligned 2D bounding box in source-image pixels [x0, y0, x1, y1], integer, with x0<=x1 and y0<=y1.

upright.description: True if the part stands on its head / upright (Kopf steht hochkant), derived from the registry face tilt. Lets the viewer flag non-flat rest poses.
